takeaway: RAG encodes the query x, retrieves the top-K passages z from a fixed document index by MIPS, lets BART generate from each passage concatenated with x, and marginalizes the per-passage predictions weighted by p_η(z|x) — once per sequence (RAG-Sequence) or once per token (RAG-Token).

reader_questions.glance: Where does the retrieved knowledge enter and how are several passages combined into one answer?
reader_questions.detail: How do RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token differ? Which parts are trained and which stay fixed?

concepts.name: Per-passage lanes merged by marginalization
concepts.takes: REPLUG Fig. 2: one lane per retrieved document whose input is the document joined with the query ([d_i | x]), the generator applied per lane, and the lanes gathered into one combined result; the combination is the warm-accented contribution.
concepts.sketch: Top row: x -> Query Encoder -> MIPS <- Document Index <- Doc Encoder <- passages (the two bi-encoder towers meet at MIPS). Bottom row: three lanes [z_k ⊕ x] -> BART -> one tall Marginalize box (both marginalizations written inside) -> y; p_η(z|x) runs from MIPS to Marginalize.

concepts.name: Retriever | memory | generator columns
concepts.takes: MuRAG Fig. 4: three columns joined by arrows labelled MIPS and Top-K, the index drawn as rows of vector + passage so the selected rows are highlighted in place.
concepts.sketch: Query encoder column -> MIPS -> index table (vectors + passages, top-K rows outlined) -> Top-K -> BART column -> y.

concepts.name: Vertical pipeline with worked example
concepts.takes: REALM Fig. 2: query text on top, retriever and generator stacked, corpus as a side note with a retrieve arrow, answer text at the bottom.
concepts.sketch: x on top -> Retriever (with index at the side) -> (x, z) -> BART -> Marginalize -> y at the bottom.

why: The contribution is the marginalization over K latent passages. REPLUG's lanes show that structure as data: every passage gets its own generator pass and the passes visibly merge into one answer, so a reader sees at a glance why K passages are retrieved and where p_η(z|x) is used. The column concept spends most of the width on the reused index, and the vertical concept hides the K-fold structure inside one box. The two-row arrangement also fits the 5.5 in NeurIPS text width.
highlight: Marginalize is the only warm (orange) element, named RAG-Sequence / RAG-Token; it gathers the three per-passage lanes and states both marginalizations in operator order (Σ_z … Π_i for RAG-Sequence, Π_i Σ_z … for RAG-Token) inside the box.

drawn_as.how: the retriever p_η(z|x) is drawn as its parts (query encoder, MIPS, document index, document encoder) under a bracket named 'Retriever p_η(z|x) (DPR)'; no box for the whole
the one BART generator p_θ (one set of parameters θ) is drawn once per passage lane (gen_1..gen_3), named by the bracket 'Generator p_θ (one shared BART) · parametric memory'

the concatenation of z with x is written into each lane's input box as '[passage title + excerpt] | x' (passage first, as in the code), so the box itself is BART's input; the joined pair enters BART gen_k, where the concat is checked
